name: Preservation to personal survival
position: Conditional project argument skeleton; not a finding
premises: A foundation retains information about a deceased individual (H-P-information).
bridge_principles: B05: the retention relation preserves the numerically same subject, not merely a representation.
An explicit identity theory establishes subjectivity beyond the bodily-life boundary.
conclusion: If both additional premises hold, H-S follows for the specified person.
strongest_objection: Information preservation can occur while the original subject ceases; duplicates expose the identity problem.
strongest_reply: Specify a subject-preserving relation rather than infer it from informational fidelity.
unresolved_issues: Truth of H-P is unassessed.
The identity relation and first-person continuation remain unresolved.

name: Endurance and enduring significance
position: Conditional project argument skeleton; not a finding
premises: A specified person or item persists under H-S or H-P.
bridge_principles: B09: persistence of that subject or item is valuable under a stated normative account.
B09: the proposed value is not defeated by the content or conditions of persistence.
conclusion: The specified persistence contributes enduring significance under those normative premises.
strongest_objection: Duration alone need not increase value, and finite value may exist without persistence.
strongest_reply: Identify the particular value preserved, such as a relationship, and argue for its normative importance.
unresolved_issues: Whether endurance is necessary, sufficient, or merely contributory must be assessed separately.
Neither objective value nor cosmic purpose follows from duration alone.

name: Conscious production to cosmic purpose
position: Conditional project argument skeleton; not a finding
premises: Conscious experience occurs within the universe, treated here as an assumed explanandum without empirical assessment.
bridge_principles: B08: an agent independently specified that outcome as an end and grounds or directs the universe toward it.
conclusion: H-I holds for that specified end if the agency and intention premises are warranted.
strongest_objection: The occurrence of an outcome is also compatible with an unintended byproduct.
strongest_reply: State ends and discriminating consequences independently of the observations being explained.
unresolved_issues: No evidence for an intending agent has been assessed.
Goodness, authority, survival and preservation remain separate.

name: Conscious foundation to moral authority
position: Conditional project argument skeleton; not a finding
premises: A proposed foundation exists and stands in specified creative or unifying relations to individuals (assumed for argument only).
bridge_principles: B10-B12: a stated normative principle connects those relations or a specified good nature to genuine reasons and obligations.
The normative principle explains binding force without identifying goodness merely with whatever the foundation does.
conclusion: H-A follows only to the extent the normative relation establishes the specified obligations.
strongest_objection: Descriptive unity, causal origin, power, or reward can leave binding moral justification unexplained.
strongest_reply: Develop a defensible good-nature or relational grounding account and compare non-theistic value/reason/obligation accounts.
unresolved_issues: Existence and goodness of the foundation are unassessed.
Objective value, moral reasons and obligations require separately explicit grounding.
Accountability and motivation do not settle authority.

name: Physicalism operational comparison
position: M-T03-PH; project stipulation, not philosopher attribution
premises: A complete physical realization account is possible.
bridge_principles: Conceptual differences need not establish ontological differences.
conclusion: Physical constitution is a viable comparator.
strongest_objection: Phenomenal character may remain unexplained.
strongest_reply: Identity or grounding need not be conceptually transparent.
unresolved_issues: Premises are unassessed. Detailed residual costs, criteria and conditional discriminators: report.md, Motivations, challenges, replies and discriminators.

name: Psychophysical laws operational comparison
position: M-T03-PL; project stipulation, not philosopher attribution
premises: Additional experiential resources may be required.
bridge_principles: General laws can explain instances without explaining their own existence.
conclusion: A constrained law model is a viable comparator.
strongest_objection: Mappings may leave their central dependence brute.
strongest_reply: Apply the same explanatory stopping rules across models.
unresolved_issues: Premises are unassessed. Detailed residual costs, criteria and conditional discriminators: report.md, Motivations, challenges, replies and discriminators.

name: Panpsychism operational comparison
position: M-T03-PA; project stipulation, not philosopher attribution
premises: Experiential constituents may support an account of complex subjects.
bridge_principles: An explicit constitutive relation can ground unified subjecthood.
conclusion: The constitutive proposal warrants comparison.
strongest_objection: Many subjects do not evidently constitute one subject.
strongest_reply: Specify and constrain a subject-constitution relation.
unresolved_issues: Premises are unassessed. Detailed residual costs, criteria and conditional discriminators: report.md, Motivations, challenges, replies and discriminators.

name: Dualism operational comparison
position: M-T03-DU; project stipulation, not philosopher attribution
premises: Subjectivity may require distinct irreducible bearers.
bridge_principles: Distinct subjects can have coherent, constrained relations to bodies.
conclusion: An explicit dualist model warrants comparison.
strongest_objection: Interaction may conflict with a complete physical causal account.
strongest_reply: Assess causal completeness and explicit interaction laws separately.
unresolved_issues: Premises are unassessed. Detailed residual costs, criteria and conditional discriminators: report.md, Motivations, challenges, replies and discriminators.

name: Idealism operational comparison
position: M-T03-ID; project stipulation, not philosopher attribution
premises: A conscious basis could ground experience and a public ordered world.
bridge_principles: A grounding model can earn support through explanatory success.
conclusion: Conscious grounding warrants comparison.
strongest_objection: Experiential knowledge does not prove mental ontology.
strongest_reply: Offer an overall explanatory argument and perspective-individuation model.
unresolved_issues: Premises are unassessed. Detailed residual costs, criteria and conditional discriminators: report.md, Motivations, challenges, replies and discriminators.

name: Theism operational comparison
position: M-T03-TH; project stipulation, not philosopher attribution
premises: Contingent reality may require explanation.
Intentional agency may provide that explanation.
bridge_principles: Independent arguments are required for agency, good ends and moral authority.
conclusion: A specified intentional creator warrants comparison.
strongest_objection: Explanation alone does not identify mind, goodness or authority.
strongest_reply: Supply distinct agency and normative arguments; test specified ends against suffering and hiddenness.
unresolved_issues: Premises are unassessed. Detailed residual costs, criteria and conditional discriminators: report.md, Motivations, challenges, replies and discriminators.

name: Functional explanation and phenomenal target
premises: Functional success.
Phenomenal target remains.
bridge_principles: Explanatory adequacy criterion.
conclusion: Further explanatory demand.
unresolved_issues: Expanded map and limits in report.md; bridges contested; no H-F/survival/theism entailment.

name: Knowledge/conceivability and modal bridge
premises: Conceivable(P and not Q).
Physicalism excludes possible(P and not Q).
conclusion: Conditional rejection of physicalism.
strongest_reply: A-T05-002 dilemma in report
unresolved_issues: Expanded map and limits in report.md; bridges contested; no H-F/survival/theism entailment.

name: Phenomenal concepts and property identity
premises: Distinct epistemic routes.
conclusion: Epistemic difference need not refute identity.
unresolved_issues: Expanded map and limits in report.md; bridges contested; no H-F/survival/theism entailment.

name: Identity and explanatory standards
premises: Identity warranted independently (conditional).
bridge_principles: B-T05-E challenged.
conclusion: No further causal connection follows.
unresolved_issues: Expanded map and limits in report.md; bridges contested; no H-F/survival/theism entailment.

name: Alexander’s brain-independence argument
position: Strongest conditional reconstruction, not endorsed conclusion
premises: Elaborate experience was remembered.
If relevant brain processes were excluded during that experience, a specified ordinary production account would fail.
Claimed external details and prior description might strengthen accuracy if independently verified.
bridge_principles: Retrospective memory accurately dates its content to the excluded interval.
Clinical evidence rules out all processes required by the targeted model.
Alternate ordinary information routes do not explain verified details.
conclusion: Conditional support for H-B; no automatic H-S/H-T or deity inference
strongest_objection: A-T06-002: neither temporal alignment nor exclusion of all relevant processing is established.
strongest_reply: Defender appeals to profound impairment, different recovery phenomenology and corroborative detail rather than credentials alone.
unresolved_issues: Recoverable brain illness is not irreversible death.
Even H-B needs a substrate definition; other physical realization is logically possible.

name: Underdetermination and ordinary alternatives
position: Audit reconstruction with Shermer’s original challenge
premises: Reports and clinical severity do not directly identify the moment each memory formed.
A feeling of reality alone cannot validate external objects.
Ordinary mechanisms may remain possible without any one being demonstrated.
bridge_principles: A claim that excludes a mechanism must establish the relevant exclusion, not rely solely on explanatory incompleteness.
conclusion: This packet does not identify a unique neural or non-neural cause
strongest_objection: A-T06-001: severe impairment and corroborated details could challenge a precisely specified brain-dependent account.
strongest_reply: Preserve corroborative reports and propose independently dated/timed tests; do not declare hallucination merely because it is possible.
unresolved_issues: Raw records and prospective synchronization absent.
Comparator studies and direct Sacks source not inspected.

name: Severe illness versus solely pharmacological coma
premises: Dittrich publishes Potter’s sedation/responsiveness account.
Mays disputes its context.
Clinical review attributes pre-sedation deterioration to illness while acknowledging mixed later contributions.
bridge_principles: Different descriptions can concern different stages and mechanisms; quotations alone do not settle physiology.
conclusion: Avoid both drug-only dismissal and inference from serious illness to complete brain inactivity
strongest_objection: Witness accounts are retrospective and contested.
strongest_reply: Published chart review strengthens severe-illness documentation but is not a continuous functional recording.
unresolved_issues: Original interview and clinical chronology needed to settle remaining particulars.

name: Conditional inference to brain independence
premises: Prospectively recruited survivors report lucid experiences; the AWARE studies report limited chart corroboration of resuscitation details.
bridge_principles: The reported experience must be independently timed to conditions excluding the neural processes required by a specified dependence model.
Ordinary information access and memory reconstruction require assessment; report accuracy alone does not supply the missing timing premise.
conclusion: These studies motivate discriminating tests but do not establish H-B in this packet.
strongest_objection: No concealed target success with established opportunity and no content-specific experience during measured absent processing are demonstrated.
strongest_reply: Incomplete measurements do not refute testimony or establish an ordinary explanation of each case.
unresolved_issues: Timing and substrate exclusion; target opportunity; irreversible death not studied.

name: Physiological and methodological countercase
position: Challenges inference to H-B without establishing physicalism
premises: AWARE II records some organized rhythms during CPR, with substantial missingness and limited montage.
Recall timing, prior knowledge, selection and ambiguous fruit-choice interpretation remain unresolved.
bridge_principles: A possible mechanism is not a demonstrated explanation of a particular account.
Aggregate EEG correlations cannot identify or causally explain an unlinked person’s reported contents.
conclusion: Brain-dependent possibilities remain open; neither physicalism nor brain independence is settled.
strongest_objection: Generic possibilities do not explain each detailed recollection.
strongest_reply: AWARE II itself acknowledges alpha-coma ambiguity and that association does not establish causation; objective participant-level testing remains necessary.
unresolved_issues: Direct post-publication author response not accessed; supplement and detailed participant data unavailable.

name: Recurrence across records and cultural settings
position: Strongest conditional case for a shared experiential phenomenon
bridge_principles: Recurrence across different documents, settings and precipitating circumstances can motivate a shared-phenomenon hypothesis when ascertainment and dependence are considered.
To infer brain independence or survival, recurrent motifs would additionally need discriminating evidence ruling out relevant ordinary information and substrate routes.
conclusion: The inspected records support investigating recurrent experiences with varied content; they do not identify a unique metaphysical cause.
strongest_objection: Shared human cognition, literary transmission, selection and coding can produce recurrence; no common clinical denominator or assured independent samples.
strongest_reply: Cultural differences do not refute every shared experiential or survival model, and these narratives predate modern NDE publicity; a constrained model must predict more than broad similarities.
unresolved_issues: No defensible likelihood ratio/posterior; English-access bias; neural timing and independent event verification absent.

name: Cultural, reporting and measurement countercase
position: Strongest countercase to invariance and direct survival inference
bridge_principles: Unequal prompts, selected reports and varying labels weaken inferences from narrative frequency to population invariance.
A content difference supports pure cultural causation only if competing physiological, experiential and reporting explanations are discriminated.
conclusion: Cultural and measurement effects remain serious alternatives; these data neither establish a purely cultural mechanism nor demonstrate a universal afterlife structure.
strongest_objection: A common experiential or afterlife reality could be interpreted differently by cultures; observational variation need not exhaust the phenomenon.
strongest_reply: That possibility is retained, but retrospective flexibility earns no distinctive predictive support without prospective constraints.
unresolved_issues: Exposure and translation not independently measured; ordinary mechanisms are possibilities rather than established causes of each episode.

name: Causal neural contributions constrain embodied mind models
premises: Site-dependent neural intervention changes reported face appearance or arousal/access markers.
Within-subject/sham/control contrasts make mere passive correlation an incomplete description.
bridge_principles: The intervention meaningfully affects the neural system relevant to the observed report/behavior.
Reports are defeasible evidence of experience; animal markers require additional validation.
conclusion: Neural processes causally contribute to embodied perception and state functions in these tested contexts; models denying any such contribution are challenged.
strongest_objection: Interventions may alter access/reporting, distributed routing or a posited interface without proving how experience is constituted.
strongest_reply: An interface account must specify predictions for the observed content, site and state effects rather than merely accommodate them.
unresolved_issues: Specific substrate versus reporting contributions.
Generalization beyond tested conditions.
Distinctive model predictions.

name: Neural dependence does not by itself settle ontology
premises: Causal modulation does not establish metaphysical identity.
Unresponsiveness and absent markers do not directly verify phenomenal absence.
Theory tests depend on biological and measurement assumptions.
bridge_principles: A metaphysical conclusion needs a discriminating prediction or an independently justified bridge.
conclusion: Results constrain embodied models without uniquely selecting physicalism or brain independence, or licensing survival claims from failures of a neural theory.
strongest_objection: An unspecified interface view can fit any data and lose predictive force against explicit neural mechanisms.
strongest_reply: Require prospective contrasting predictions; logical underdetermination does not make alternatives equally supported.
unresolved_issues: Neural necessity across states.
Conscious versus unconscious processing.
Independent identity and survival criteria.

name: Mechanism and agency compatibility
premises: A mechanism explains how a process operates.
An agent explanation can concern why that process was arranged.
bridge_principles: B-T10-01: Distinct explanatory relations can coexist if their substantive causal claims do not conflict.
conclusion: A mechanism alone does not exclude agency; positive support requires an additional comparison.
strongest_objection: Observed human artifact origins do not establish cosmic agency.
strongest_reply: Unobserved causes can be inferred; require a discriminatory reason rather than direct observation as an absolute rule.
unresolved_issues: Closure assumptions for specific models
Positive evidence for agency

name: Intelligibility and rational origin
premises: Discoverable mathematical order is the explanandum.
A specified rational creator has independently motivated reasons to enable inquiry.
The proposed order is less expected under a defined impersonal comparison.
bridge_principles: B-T10-02: Better independently motivated expectations can supply abductive support.
conclusion: If these comparisons hold, intelligibility favors the specified rational-origin model.
strongest_objection: Agent preferences and contrast class may be fitted after observing the world; impersonal structure and learning may also explain fit.
strongest_reply: A common rational source may unify broad mathematical order and our capacity to grasp it beyond local adaptation.
unresolved_issues: Actual comparative expectations
Limits of human analogy
Empirical cognitive alternatives not tested
Discovery versus intrinsic law ontology

name: Contingent reality and necessary concrete ground
premises: Contingent concrete totality is a legitimate contingent explanandum.
Every such contingent fact has an adequate explanation.
A complete explanation cannot be wholly internal, circular or another member of the contingent totality.
Concrete reality ultimately needs a concrete explanatory ground.
bridge_principles: B-T10-03: PSR extends to the specified contingent totality.
B-T10-04: External adequate explanation plus concrete-ground requirement excludes a wholly contingent or merely abstract ultimate basis.
conclusion: The ultimate explanatory basis includes necessary concrete reality; mind does not yet follow.
strongest_objection: Local explanations may exhaust the legitimate demand; necessary impersonal reality remains possible.
strongest_reply: Local causal links can leave why the totality obtains unanswered; exemptions from PSR need justification.
unresolved_issues: Totality contingency
PSR scope
Abstract versus concrete grounding
Necessity-to-intellect
Nonnecessitating explanation and modal collapse

name: Fine-tuning comparative support
premises: E is specified life-permitting evidence.
D independently specifies an agent with reasons to produce embodied conscious life.
N specifies an impersonal alternative with less expectation of E.
Common background B and observation selection are handled consistently.
bridge_principles: B-T10-05: A larger likelihood for E under D than under N comparatively supports D; posterior odds also depend on prior odds.
conclusion: E conditionally favors D over N; this alone establishes neither an overall posterior nor the full conscious-foundation package.
strongest_objection: Sensitivity does not fix a probability measure; a designer’s choice of laws and the evidential role of life are underdetermined.
strongest_reply: Qualitative orderings can matter without exact numbers; initial life may be evidence, and unexplained cause complexity need not erase a likelihood advantage.
unresolved_issues: Physics not independently audited
Measure/parameterization/correlations
Agent preferences
Multiverse and deeper-law comparisons
Old evidence and selection
Missing Collins appendix

name: Incremental stringency and divine indifference
position: conditional objection to a class of design arguments
premises: Life O is already in background.
Design and nondesign induce the same distribution over O-compatible possibilities after conditioning.
bridge_principles: B-T10-06: Matching conditional distributions assign equal probability to the same stringency event.
conclusion: Under the matching assumptions, stringency adds no further design support once life is known.
strongest_objection: Divine and impersonal processes may justify different measures; ignorance alone is not uniformity.
strongest_reply: An argument relying on indifference must justify its asymmetric application; imposing matching distributions is an internal challenge, not an empirical law.
unresolved_issues: Independently motivated asymmetric preferences
Choice of possibility space
Full original White/Bradley exchange and later replies

name: Physical time without a metaphysical shortcut
premises: Einstein’s relations preserve clock order.
Rovelli’s histories and relational predictions survive removal of privileged external time.
bridge_principles: A formal representation does not determine the full ontology of what it represents.
conclusion: These results do not establish a timeless conscious bearer.
strongest_objection: An all-history representation may naturally motivate eternalist ontology.
strongest_reply: Even eternalism contains earlier/later relations and does not identify a single experiencing mind.
unresolved_issues: Interpretative merits of eternalism and rival ontologies remain open.
No broad quantum-gravity or empirical-relativity review.

name: A timeless conscious foundation with temporal manifestation
premises: Suppose a conscious ground can know ordered contents in one non-discursive act.
Suppose a non-temporal grounding relation can explain why a concrete history obtains.
Suppose individual perspectives are grounded without requiring additions to the ground.
bridge_principles: Explanatory and intentional priority need not be temporal priority.
A timeless intention can be directed toward a whole history and its ends.
conclusion: Under these substantive assumptions M2 avoids the simple accumulation contradiction and could unify temporal order with conscious grounding.
strongest_objection: The model may redescribe history without explaining its concrete existence or subjective individuation; a fixed act may not count as agency.
strongest_reply: It posits an actual subject and reasons-guided dependence, rather than merely an abstract record; the absence of deliberation does not by definition exclude intention.
unresolved_issues: Prove the proposed grounding relation intelligible and explanatory.
Supply comparative reason to prefer mind over impersonal structure.
Value and goodness require separate premises.

name: The tensed-knowledge challenge
premises: Suppose objective presentness is irreducible.
Suppose perfect knowledge must encompass which events are presently occurring.
Suppose tracking these changing truths requires intrinsic cognitive succession.
bridge_principles: The presence of irreducibly tensed reality, not mere temporal order, drives the inference.
conclusion: Then a cognitively perfect ground of this temporal world cannot meet H-T.
strongest_objection: A defender denies absolute presentness or argues one atemporal act knows every tensed fact through a non-successive access relation.
strongest_reply: The first response rejects a key premise and is a serious alternative; the second must explain access without either missing changing actuality or collapsing all times into one temporal present.
unresolved_issues: Neither A-theory nor B-theory settled here.
Direct modern defender originals and response chain remain coverage gaps.
Propositional and non-propositional knowledge need separate accounts.

name: Timeless personhood and intentional responsiveness
premises: Necessary conditions of personhood must not be inferred solely from the way finite humans learn.
A possible knower may have self-awareness and rational volition without deliberative updating.
Responsiveness can be specified as dependence of effects on reasons, or as newly acquired awareness; these differ.
bridge_principles: A capacity can remain unexercised; possible temporal exercise does not show the bearer already has succession.
conclusion: Simple personhood arguments do not automatically refute timelessness; actual interaction still needs a model.
strongest_objection: The proposed timeless capacities may be nominal; responsiveness to genuinely new events seems to require new states.
strongest_reply: Either justify whole-history reasons-sensitive dependence, or accept a temporal divine life with creation. Neither option is cost-free.
unresolved_issues: Craig’s timeless-without-creation scope is limited.
Transition into time must not posit a time before time.
Trinitarian illustration is an additional theological assumption, not universal-subject evidence.

name: Whole-history preservation versus survival
premises: Representing or including all events of a finite life preserves specified contents.
T01 H-S requires the same person’s subjectivity beyond irreversible bodily death.
bridge_principles: A record or a containing knower is not automatically numerically identical to the represented person.
conclusion: M3 inclusion alone supplies a preservation proposal, not H-S.
strongest_objection: An enlarged subject-history might include genuinely continuing subjectivity outside embodied succession.
strongest_reply: That is a distinct stronger hypothesis deserving assessment under an explicit identity relation; merely calling it inclusion does not establish it.
unresolved_issues: T13: bearer, death condition, numerical identity, continuation domain, memory and branching.

name: Identity and physical realization
premises: Experience and its causal relations require explanation.
A single property may be accessible through different concepts.
Empirical causal evidence can warrant identification if rivals are adequately excluded.
bridge_principles: B-T12-ID: concept difference need not imply property difference.
B-T12-WARRANT: an identity still needs evidence; physical closure cannot be assumed from correlation.
conclusion: Physical identity/grounding is a live explanatory strategy, not disproved by epistemic difference alone.
strongest_objection: The account may capture reporting or causal role without phenomenal character.
strongest_reply: Identity theorist denies two items remain to be bridged once identity is warranted; separate epistemic access need not add a property.
unresolved_issues: Does the identification capture the target?
What empirical/semantic premises warrant the identity?
Weak emergence needs a realization account and subject boundary.
construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

name: Experiential bases and subject constitution
premises: Phenomenality is real.
Suppose physical description leaves intrinsic role-realizers open.
Suppose experiential role-realizers jointly constitute ordinary subjects.
bridge_principles: B-T12-R: experience realizes physical roles rather than intervening from outside.
B-T12-COMB: base properties and relations sufficiently ground a bounded subject.
conclusion: Experiential bases could integrate phenomenality and causal roles without extra macro-level intervention.
strongest_objection: Microexperiences plus physics may not necessitate another subject; palette and structure constraints are distinct.
strongest_reply: The complete base can include phenomenal relations; informational rather than geometrical structure may matter. Inconceivability/impossibility is not established.
unresolved_issues: Specify relation and boundaries without arbitrary selection.
Conceivability-to-possibility standard must match its use against physicalism.
Emergent macroexperience changes the constitutive model and restores causal/law costs.
construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

name: Naturalistic property dualism and causal/epistemic cost
position: PL1, with PL2 and substance variants differentiated
premises: Suppose phenomenal reality is not wholly physically grounded.
Regular psychophysical principles could explain particular experiential distributions.
Basic properties and laws can be legitimate explanatory stopping points.
bridge_principles: B-T12-L: irreducibility warrants this law model only with additional grounding argument.
B-T12-EPI: law-based reliability/acquaintance can justify beliefs without experience causing physical reports (proposed reply, not established).
conclusion: A psychophysical-law model is a distinct serious alternative; it neither entails a separable person nor removes its epistemic burden.
strongest_objection: Under closure and no overdetermination, distinct experiential influence threatens exclusion; epiphenomenalism threatens experience-based knowledge/reporting.
strongest_reply: PL1 appeals to lawful tracking and direct acquaintance without extra physical effects; PL2 instead questions closure and proposes interaction laws. Neither reply is simply a conservation-law refutation.
unresolved_issues: Why this mapping rather than another?
Would a tracking account secure truth/justification or only matching reports?
Interaction/substance variants lack inspected direct defender/reply chains in this packet.
construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

name: Dissociated cosmic idealism
premises: Experience supplies a known kind of concrete reality.
Suppose a shared conscious ground supports mutually constrained private perspectives.
Suppose bodies/world are extrinsic appearances of those relations.
bridge_principles: B-T12-DISS: selective cognitive access must ground finite phenomenality, not just block communication.
B-T12-APP: an appearance relation must recover exact neural interventions and public regularities.
conclusion: The model offers a unified candidate explanation if dissociation, manifestation and law constraints are independently justified.
strongest_objection: An analogy to dissociation in embodied people does not establish cosmic subject division; calling brain activity an appearance can merely redescribe data.
strongest_reply: Distinguish inaccessible contents from nonexistent contents and causal impingement from shared cognitive access; formulate one lawful shared environment rather than personal wishing.
unresolved_issues: Cosmic extension of analogy and clinical premises unverified.
Organism-scale boundary needs noncircular criterion and edge cases.
Specific laws and mapping not derived; shared substrate not automatically shared perceptions.
construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

name: Cosmic constitution versus plural idealism
premises: Suppose a whole can be ontologically prior to local structures.
An experiential whole might realize physical roles.
Human perspectives require either identity-with-modes or distinct grounded subjects.
bridge_principles: B-T12-WHOLE: physical holism alone does not select an experiential ground.
B-T12-SUBJ: shared bearer, shared type of reality and numerical identity are different claims.
conclusion: Whole-first models relocate constitution rather than automatically solving it; plural idealism need not entail one universal subject.
strongest_objection: One subject cannot be numerically identical to multiple mutually distinct subjects under ordinary identity logic.
strongest_reply: Identity version relativizes access to modes; nonidentity version posits constitutive dependence. Plural idealism permits multiple basic subjects with lawful coordination.
unresolved_issues: Identity/mode view revises ordinary individuality.
Nonidentity grounding needs a sufficient principle.
Plural coordination and basic intersubject relations carry separate costs.
None establishes H-S or H-T.
construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

name: Psychological appropriation and a repaired continuity criterion
premises: A person is self-aware across relevant stages.
Past experience can be appropriately appropriated despite changing matter.
bridge_principles: Specify causal continuity without presupposing identity; add branching policy.
conclusion: Such continuity is a candidate basis for same-person persistence.
strongest_objection: Memories may duplicate, disappear or presuppose ownership.
strongest_reply: Project repair: overlapping causal links and a nonbranching clause avoid direct-memory transitivity failure; they still need independent justification.
unresolved_issues: Not all modern continuity accounts inspected; Parfit direct access failed.
Locke’s own theory is not identical to this repaired project model.

name: Thinking animal and biological persistence
premises: A human organism is present.
It thinks.
There is exactly one relevant thinker and that thinker is the person.
bridge_principles: Identity preserves the organism’s genuine persistence conditions, once specified.
conclusion: The human person is that organism; a disembodied copy alone does not preserve it.
strongest_objection: A transplanted cerebrum seems to carry the person; or the strict thinker is a soul/constituted subject.
strongest_reply: Olson presses costs of denying organism thought or multiplying thinkers; psychological evidence/concern may be mistaken for constitution.
unresolved_issues: Unique-thinker and strict animal-thinking premises contested.
Animalism alone is not a complete theory of death, resurrection or animal persistence.

name: Simple subject through qualitative change
premises: A hypothetical split leaves two equally psychologically supported candidates.
There is a determinate fact about which, if either, is the earlier subject beyond the total qualitative facts.
bridge_principles: Indeterminacy of accessible evidence reflects an additional bearer fact.
That fact requires an immaterial essential part.
conclusion: A soul is the candidate identity bearer.
strongest_objection: Epistemic underdetermination does not entail an immaterial entity; deny further-fact premise or specify a physical/causal identity rule.
strongest_reply: Charitable project reply: first-person numerical identity is not exhausted by descriptive similarity; the defender must argue that fact is real and immaterial, not merely unknowable.
unresolved_issues: Short essay does not resolve all technical objections.
A surviving soul and continuing experience require additional persistence/activation premises; simplicity is not immortality.

name: Enlarged first-person history beyond bodily life
premises: The foundation grounds a concrete first-person history, not merely an information record.
The history includes subjectivity outside the embodied-life boundary.
A defended relation unifies those portions as the same person.
bridge_principles: Ordered content can be grounded without successive changes in the foundation.
An explicit criterion—not resemblance alone—licenses same-subject attribution.
conclusion: M2 or enlargedM3 could satisfy H-S with foundation-level H-T.
strongest_objection: The asserted ownership/extension may restate survival; a universal knower can preserve a finite life without the person continuing.
strongest_reply: Treat subjectivity and individuation as substantive ontology with identifiable constraints; this blocks dismissal by definition but adds explanatory/evidential costs.
unresolved_issues: No observation here establishes enlarged history.
Strict organism criterion rejects disembodied extension unless same-organism relation defended.
Timeless individual model must explain non-successive awareness; the temporal-individual model does not solve that separate issue.

name: Temporal phenomenology under competing interpretations
premises: Altered-time reports are documented as reports.
Composite instruments mix distinct phenomenologies.
Drug-context scale overlap is observed in one bounded design.
bridge_principles: Phenomenological resemblance alone does not identify mechanism or ontology.
conclusion: The reports motivate investigation but do not discriminate H-T/H-S without timing, identity and access evidence.
strongest_objection: Survival interpretation: coherent first-person reports and striking information may reveal real access beyond the body; instruments may miss their distinctiveness.
strongest_reply: Ordinary alternative has demonstrated drug-context overlap, while the survival reply correctly notes that inducing a resemblance need not explain a given case. Seek prospective, independently scored information and resolved timing; separately ask what identity relation it supports.
unresolved_issues: No same-mechanism conclusion; no inference of equal support.
No result here crosses irreversible bodily death under H-S.

name: Enduring significance: necessity versus enhancement
premises: Relationships, understanding and achieved goods can be worth preserving.
Specified continuation retains the same subjects and relevant goods.
Additional worthwhile experience is available without overriding harm.
bridge_principles: Comparative enhancement needs a defensible value ordering.
Necessity additionally needs total loss to defeat all significance in the selected domain.
conclusion: Endurance can enhance significance under these premises; necessity and actuality require more.
strongest_objection: Finite goods may retain value even when no one later remembers; endless continuation may damage what mattered.
strongest_reply: A defender can argue continued shared life is an additional relational good, not merely a record, while defending separately the stronger non-loss requirement.
unresolved_issues: Value ordering; whose goods; identity; extent of duration; no inferred actual survival

name: Finite value with an acknowledged cosmic remainder
premises: A finite instance of learning, care or relief can benefit actual subjects.
The worth of that benefit need not depend entirely on subsequent recognition.
bridge_principles: Non-erasure principle: later absence alone does not retroactively make every earlier benefit worthless.
conclusion: Finite meaning can be real on this account while cosmic intention and enduring significance remain separate questions.
strongest_objection: A meaningful episode may still lack an ultimately worthwhile setting; all loss can defeat the hoped-for relationship to a larger whole.
strongest_reply: Distinguish missing further goods from nonexistence of prior goods; do not claim this answers the larger purpose question.
unresolved_issues: Ground of objective value; relation of local to whole-life value; criterion of ultimate significance

name: Williams on categorical desire and immortal life, with Fischer’s reply
position: Inspected original challenge and reply, with project adjudication
premises: Williams: categorical desires can give present reasons to continue, independently of merely avoiding frustration.
Williams: an adequate immortal prospect must preserve the person and relate appropriately to the aims motivating survival.
Williams argues extended fixed-character life undermines motivation, while disjoint or radically accumulated lives fail to solve the appropriate-relation problem.
bridge_principles: The author’s modal step generalizes from conditions of recognizably human character to endless human existence; this remains contested.
A burden about appropriate prospective concern is distinct from numerical identity and from objective worth.
conclusion: Williams supplies a stronger challenge than mere hedonic boredom, but its universal necessity is not established by the present comparison; conditional worthwhile endurance remains open.
strongest_objection: Fischer allows varied activities, appropriately spaced repeatable pleasures, and acceptable character development; absorbed attention need not eliminate ownership. These contest inevitable exhaustion and indiscriminate identity-loss claims.
strongest_reply: A strengthened Williams-side response asks whether renewal preserves genuine engagement and prospective reasons rather than simply suppressing awareness of impoverishment. Occasional pleasantness does not settle that question, and every experience being owned does not by itself establish an adequate relation to present aims.
unresolved_issues: Whether human categorical projects necessarily exhaust under all relevant immortal arrangements
Whether relational development can renew motivation while preserving identity and appropriate concern
Fischer’s repeatability/variety response does not alone establish objective worth or infinite resources
Williams addresses endless human life; application to strict timeless foundation or transformed persons needs additional premises

name: Cosmic purpose and normative worth
position: Strong purpose account with bridge audit
premises: An agent intends a stated end for a specified cosmic domain.
Its causal or grounding contribution explains why that domain has relevant features.
The end and agent-person relation are normatively worthwhile.
bridge_principles: Intentional explanation requires independent warrant for intention and constraints.
Authorship supplies a purpose relation, not worth by definition.
conclusion: A worthy intentional relation can add cosmic significance conditionally; observed conscious production alone does not establish it.
strongest_objection: Arbitrary or harmful ends would still be purposes; a timeless agent model owes coherent intention; designer premises remain unsupported.
strongest_reply: Specify a loving creator-person relation and whole-history intention, or temporal agency; assess these with the same standards as rival primitive laws and value commitments.
unresolved_issues: Actual intention; agency model; normative foundation; domain; goodness and authority deferred

name: Consciousness-factory discrimination
premises: Production, development and preservation are different proposed ends.
Each end is paired with a declared population, means, constraints and tradeoffs.
bridge_principles: Outcomes weaken a model only when excluded or disfavored by those fixed commitments.
Observer selection and shared premises must be included.
conclusion: Precisely constrained variants can face qualitative tests; unrestricted hidden purposes discriminate weakly.
strongest_objection: Unknown goals/resources can accommodate almost any outcome; conscious observers necessarily observe from a conscious perspective.
strongest_reply: Precommit to independent goals, inclusion rules and feasible alternatives; compare the same data across intentional, impersonal-teleological and incidental models.
unresolved_issues: No population survey or likelihoods; no completed test; suffering analysis deferred to T15

name: From conscious value to moral authority
premises: There are subjects to whom conditions can be good or bad.
Assume reasons to protect subjects are objective, not merely reports of desire.
Propose one necessarily good personal foundation whose relation to agents grounds binding demands.
bridge_principles: Valence or flourishing has normative significance.
Relevant others count even when helping them conflicts with my aims.
The foundation is the relevant good, and its relation supplies legitimate authority.
Commands are identifiable and consistent with that nature.
conclusion: The full account could unify welfare, reasons, obligations and accountability if every bridge is warranted; consciousness alone proves none of the later bridges.
strongest_objection: Calling a being good or creative may presuppose the normativity being explained; unity and sanctions can yield only self-interest.
strongest_reply: Grounding need not be a definition or a temporal production: a defensible identity/constitution account can terminate explanation in a necessary good and a legitimate relation. This reply still owes warrant for that identity and relation.
unresolved_issues: No derivation of impartiality from mere awareness.
No independent authority proof in inspected Craig transcript.
No assumption that divine commands all have identical modal status.
authorship: Project-authored reconstruction; source attributions confined to linked claims.

name: Secular moral objectivity and its explanatory costs
position: Positive naturalistic account with other secular families retained
premises: Human and animal conditions can affect their interests independently of current approval.
A proposed moral standard considers all affected interests impartially.
Correctness can diverge from present preference and social convention.
bridge_principles: Identify the proposed natural property with normative goodness or rightness, with semantic and explanatory warrant.
Justify impartiality and the treatment of conflicting interests.
conclusion: A physicalist ontology has a substantive route to moral realism; this route remains contested and does not settle every categorical-reason demand.
strongest_objection: A fully informed egoist may still reject impartiality; reliable preference explanation might explain moral belief while omitting moral authority.
strongest_reply: Separate truth and applicability from the agent’s motivation; evaluate whether the proposed identity explains correction, practical criticism and disagreement. Other secular accounts can instead take categorical reasons or rational agency as basic, with their own costs.
unresolved_issues: Naturalism is not a proof from evolution.
Constructivism and non-natural realism reconstructed in matrix but no decisive original defender inspected.
Aggregative criterion may face rights, comparability and determinate-idealization objections.
authorship: Project-authored reconstruction; source attributions confined to linked claims.

name: Suffering as evidence against specified perfect governance
position: Evidential challenge, distinct from bare logical incompatibility
premises: Assume an agent knows the relevant harms and feasible alternatives, can prevent them and is perfectly good.
Some suffering appears to lack a permission-justifying dependence on goods or avoidance of comparable evil.
bridge_principles: Our inability to find such dependence is defeasible evidence of its absence in the relevant domain.
A perfectly good agent does not permit harms without adequate justification; equal-value and irreplaceability qualifications must be specified.
conclusion: Suffering challenges that attribute package if the evidential and normative premises hold; it is not a deduction from the mere occurrence of any evil.
strongest_objection: Our sample of goods, causal relations and feasible worlds may be too limited to assess what an omniscient being could justifiably permit.
strongest_reply: Finite limits do not automatically erase all evidence; compare what each hypothesis actually leads us to expect and what independently supports claimed limitations. Theistic countergrounds can rationally matter.
unresolved_issues: No measured prevalence or likelihood supplied.
A hypothetical animal does not establish an actual event.
Free-will and soul-making originals beyond the inspected discussions remain gaps.
authorship: Project-authored reconstruction; source attributions confined to linked claims.

name: Restoration of persons and justification of harm
position: Strong enduring-restoration reply and victim-centered challenge
premises: Assume the same victims continue and receive goods capable of restoring meaningful lives.
Assume their harms can be integrated without denying their reality or replacing victims with successors.
bridge_principles: A good total life or meaningful integration can answer some questions about final loss.
Antecedent permission requires a separate justification, including necessity, proportionality, rights and alternatives where applicable.
conclusion: Restoration can improve an account of what becomes of victims, while an account of why harms were permitted remains independently contestable.
strongest_objection: A later good may quiet grief without making the original injustice permissible; one person’s reconciliation cannot speak for another victim.
strongest_reply: The strongest version addresses each victim and distinguishes redemption from approval of wrongdoing; an internal consistency defense may use its own independently specified goods without claiming their actual existence is thereby proved.
unresolved_issues: The possibility and worth of divine intimacy remain contested.
Identity and temporal manifestation must be specified.
Adams’s later clarifications and reply to Sutherland not inspected.
authorship: Project-authored reconstruction; source attributions confined to linked claims.

name: Nonresistant nonbelief and relationship
position: Hiddenness challenge with a bounded, currently reconstructed reply
premises: Assume perfect love includes being open to conscious reciprocal relationship with each capable person.
Assume belief in the other’s existence is required for that specified relationship.
Assume some capable persons lack belief for causes unrelated to resisting that relationship.
bridge_principles: Perfect love entails that availability at each relevant time, rather than only eventual welfare or eventual access.
conclusion: If the premises hold, the specified perfectly loving personal God is excluded; other ultimate foundations remain open.
strongest_objection: Howard-Snyder distinguishes a desire for relationship now from an overriding reason to enable it now. Even a well-disposed inculpable seeker might benefit from owning or refining the disposition to love. He offers defeasible prima facie reasons and epistemic caution, not proof of actual divine reasons.
strongest_reply: Project comparison: a possible counterfactual disposition is not automatically resistance causing present nonbelief. Ask whether improving love can occur in an available relationship, and whether delaying access is no worse than other means once the lost relationship is counted. A defender may contest that comparison or our knowledge of it. Note18 and reply4 identify limits to this particular defense; no blanket victory is inferred.
unresolved_issues: The1996reply addresses earlier Schellenberg; the2025argument emphasizes nonresistance causally relevant to nonbelief. Exact earlier book/reply exchange not inspected.
A reason to delay developing a relationship does not automatically explain withholding the conditions of being open to one; this is the contested bridge.
No observed distribution of dispositions or actual divine permission reasons.
Availability, fittingness and the no-worse-alternative criterion remain disputed.
authorship: Project-authored reconstruction; source attributions confined to linked claims.

name: Goodness, authority and dependence across the package
premises: Value judgments support the moral-grounding proposal and also underwrite evil objections.
Knowledge of goodness and permission-justifying reasons can have different scope.
Claims of actual survival or intended moral education need evidence apart from their usefulness in a reply.
bridge_principles: Avoid counting the same moral premise as independent evidence each time it recurs.
Apply explanatory stopping-point and epistemic-access standards symmetrically to divine and secular accounts.
conclusion: This packet maps burdens for H-G and H-A, with conditional effects on H-I/P/S; it identifies neither a numerical posterior nor a winning full metaphysics.
strongest_objection: Restricting knowledge of unknown goods need not undermine simple moral knowledge; criticism can demand unreasonable omniscience of the defender.
strongest_reply: Use local rather than blanket skepticism and name what remains knowable; test whether the positive and negative inferences genuinely rely on the same inaccessible domain.
unresolved_issues: No equal-support verdict.
Removing retrospective NDE claims leaves conceptual distinctions but no new survival evidence.
Rejecting moral realism changes the moral argument and some evil formulations; internal inconsistency arguments can still use an opponent’s commitments.
authorship: Project-authored reconstruction; source attributions confined to linked claims.

name: Dentures conditional anomalous-perception argument
premises: In Smit’s translated nurse account, the patient later identifies TG and a distinctive cart/shelf associated with the dentures; investigators did not obtain a direct patient interview.
Smit and Rivas acknowledge dependence on one principal witness and state that official medical records had been destroyed; the present audit has no measured EEG interval for the dentures perception.
Smit and Rivas reply that TG placed dentures removal before restarting the Thumper, and that a pre-opened wooden shelf undermines an explanation relying on hearing a metal drawer.
bridge_principles: A verified acquisition episode incompatible with a specified dependence model challenges that model only when timing, identity and information-access premises hold.
conclusion: If the report and exclusion/timing premises hold, the specific neural-dependence model would be challenged.
strongest_objection: Single-witness retrospective timing and information control are insufficient to establish those premises.
strongest_reply: Unusual shelf details and pre-Thumper removal deserve testing; a generic ordinary possibility does not erase the report.
unresolved_issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.

name: Reynolds conditional anomalous-perception argument
premises: Carter reproduces Reynolds’s descriptions of a toothbrush-like surgical tool, its case, a vessel-size exchange and an apparent encounter with relatives; the narrative and subsequent matching depend substantially on Sabom’s account.

Carter explicitly places the externally checkable early perceptions before absent brainstem response; Hameroff conditionally agrees the four auditory examples occurred under anesthesia rather than hypothermic circulatory arrest.

Carter argues that vivid visual details, the missing reported clicks, sealing/masking and brainstem-versus-conscious perception distinctions challenge Woerlee’s account, and proposes a calibrated reconstruction.

Carter quotes Cordova on technical parameters and explicitly locates Cordova in the adjacent operating room; Cordova’s quoted statement calls for an experiment and does not itself establish whether Reynolds heard.
bridge_principles: A verified acquisition episode incompatible with a specified dependence model challenges that model only when timing, identity and information-access premises hold.
conclusion: If precise perception and independently established exclusion conditions coincide, the case favors acquisition beyond the specified normal channels.
strongest_objection: Checkable claims occur outside the alleged standstill interval, and drug/monitoring/access conditions are incompletely inspected.
strongest_reply: Carter’s technical details and visual specificity challenge simplistic hearing reconstructions; neither party has supplied the decisive controlled comparison here.
unresolved_issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.

name: Limit of survival and cosmic extrapolation
premises: The two dossiers support specific, traceable perception claims and substantive disputes, but lack independently fixed perception timing plus complete information-access controls needed to identify extracerebral acquisition.
Resuscitation reports do not by themselves establish the same person’s subjectivity beyond irreversible death, fundamental mind, universal subjecthood or timelessness.
bridge_principles: Temporary independence does not automatically establish irreversible-death survival or cosmic/normative attributes.
conclusion: Neither dossier establishes the full enduring/timeless conscious-foundation package.
strongest_objection: A verified brain-independent episode could nevertheless be relevant to models permitting personal survival.
strongest_reply: Relevance is retained conditionally; irreversible death, numerical identity, universal subjecthood, purpose and normative relations require additional premises.
unresolved_issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.

name: Causally generated nonstructural experience
premises: Experiences have characteristics and causal relevance warranting explanation.
Organized physical systems causally support experience.
Experiential properties can be basic and nonstructural without being separate substances.
bridge_principles: Causal production does not by itself establish constitutive reduction.
Qualified causal completeness of an exclusively nonexperiential account is denied.
conclusion: A causal-emergent model is available as a distinct proposal; its actuality is not established.
strongest_objection: The complete microphysical causal story might explain all effects; first-person access may not reveal hidden constitution.
strongest_reply: Specify emergents as intermediate causes; compare latent-powers alternatives fairly.
unresolved_issues: Phenomenal irreducibility premise
Generation and subject laws
Independent discriminatory evidence

name: Noncausal-base causal preemption
premises: An irreducible emergent has a sufficient basal condition.
The base-to-emergent determination is noncausal.
Emergent influence must act through later basal conditions.
bridge_principles: A sufficient basal causal explanation preempts an independent irreducible causal competitor absent acceptable overdetermination.
conclusion: Emergent properties face causal and explanatory exclusion under the stated dependence assumptions.
strongest_objection: The base may act through an emergent causal intermediary, or mere necessitation may not bestow the relevant powers.
strongest_reply: The selected argument rules out a causal intermediary by its noncausal emergence premise; alternative dependence accounts need separate evaluation.
unresolved_issues: Justification and scope of noncausal-base premise
Causal versus nomic sufficiency

name: Temporal causal-chain reply
premises: Physical configuration generates and sustains an emergent over time.
The emergent mediates some later effects.
There is no independently complete parallel physical route in the model.
bridge_principles: Earlier causal dependence does not automatically eliminate intermediate causal relevance.
conclusion: Kim's selected preemption inference does not establish a contradiction in this revised model without its disputed premises.
strongest_objection: Relabeling the mechanism may add no explanatory benefit over latent microphysical powers.
strongest_reply: The authors contest simplicity and offer a history-dependent scenario; this motivates comparison without settling it.
unresolved_issues: Actuality and causal laws
Simplicity disagreement
Strongest microdispositional alternative

name: Micro-latent powers and property individuation
position: Shoemaker countercase and reply to Kim
premises: Micro-latent powers manifest only in suitable combinations.
Complete microfacts, including those powers, fix macrofacts.
On the preferred view properties possess their individuating causal features essentially.
bridge_principles: Nomic necessitation alone need not constitute the relevant causal power in the provisional distinct-property account.
Under preferred individuation and noncausal dependence, equivalent causal properties are identical.
conclusion: A response to preemption can support a microstructural or descriptive account instead of basic nonstructural emergence.
strongest_objection: The individuation assumptions may be disputed; the 2005 model changes the dependence relation and contests the rival's simplicity.
strongest_reply: Shoemaker explicitly considers a causal-base option before rejecting it from his essential-powers commitments; the disagreement remains premise-dependent.
unresolved_issues: Causal essentialism not independently adjudicated
Latent-power laws unspecified for actual consciousness
Later Shoemaker/Shrader debate uninspected

name: Lowe’s subject and intentional-causation model
bridge_principles: Identity criteria for a subject differ from criteria for its changing body or parts.
The relevant decision and ramifying neural aggregate have different counterfactual profiles.
conclusion: On those commitments, distinct subjects can explain intentional action while physical event chains remain complete.
strongest_objection: A physically sufficient event also fixes that it occurs; relabeling the intentional explanandum as a fact does not by itself remove competing sufficiency. Unity experienced in deciding does not independently settle causal event individuation.
strongest_reply: Lowe can challenge extension of event closure to facts and distinguish the type of intended outcome from its token realization. This works only with justified distinctions and counterfactuals.
unresolved_issues: Justification of distinct identity conditions
Distinct causal contribution without duplication
Empirical adequacy of the neural/event premises
No observed postmortem continuation

name: Bennett’s conditional exclusion challenge
position: Nonreductive physicalist challenge to dualist compatibility
bridge_principles: Ordinary independent sufficient causes differ from dependent causal descriptions.
Relevant closest-world counterfactuals retain enough background to test genuine causal independence.
conclusion: A dualist with merely contingent psychophysical links needs a different response than the physicalist dependence strategy, unless a defensible necessitating relation is supplied.
strongest_objection: The decisive modal test may sever an explanatory embodiment relation and thereby test a different causal situation; metaphysical necessitation is not conceded to physicalism alone.
strongest_reply: A relation must explain the dependence and have independent motivation; arbitrary covariance cannot be stipulated into the fixed counterfactual background. Bennett also leaves completeness itself as a separate dualist dispute.
unresolved_issues: Conditional completeness
Admissible counterfactual background
Coherence and motivation of necessary relations between distinct substances

name: Engelhardt’s inclusive compatibility reply
position: Revised substance dualism with dependent property sharing
bridge_principles: Two property bearers need not supply two independently sufficient physical pushes.
Counterfactual comparison should preserve a well-founded explanatory embodiment relation.
conclusion: A specified substance-dualist variant can contest the inference from two bearers to systematic independent overdetermination.
strongest_objection: Token sharing and embodiment may merely restate the dependence to be explained; if their modal force is unsupported, exclusion returns. A model that surrenders distinctive independent powers may not meet Lowe’s original explanatory ambition.
strongest_reply: Require a relation with explanatory standing comparable to relations accepted in physicalist constitution cases; do not assume numerical distinctness entails causal independence.
unresolved_issues: Distinct colocated bearers
One property instance with multiple bearers
Independent tests of embodiment
No independently distinctive powers or empirical advantage established

name: Reflective agency and the proposed authority of humanity
bridge_principles: Acting reflectively requires a normative practical identity.
The value of contingent identities depends on valuing humanity as their necessary source.
Reasons are inherently shareable in a way that supports interpersonal demands.
conclusion: If these bridges hold, reflective agents owe moral obligations that do not depend merely on contingent desires.
strongest_objection: A need for some reason or self-conception does not yet establish an impartial moral reason; public intelligibility may leave agent-relative authority intact.
strongest_reply: The proposed result is not an inference from private egoistic reasons to public ones; it challenges the assumed privacy and reconstructs principles constitutive of reflective agency.
unresolved_issues: Necessity of normative identity for action
Value of a condition versus condition of valuing
Humanity-wide domain and binding publicity
Concrete duty content, conflict and complete skepticism

name: Nagel’s direct challenge to law and identity grounding
position: Realist rival within the selected exchange
bridge_principles: Reflection can reveal evaluative reasons rather than create them.
A general rule can remain egoistic; regularity alone does not establish causal agency.
conclusion: The constructive account needs an additional justification of its law-like and interpersonal requirements, and may reverse the direction of normative explanation.
strongest_objection: Treating reflection as an already impersonal standpoint may assume the generality it seeks to justify; locating reasons in a standpoint does not alone settle whether they are discovered or constructed.
strongest_reply: Evaluate the actual reasons for treating persons’ interests as significant; moral concern need not be replaced by a self-image or payoff.
unresolved_issues: Independent warrant for the evaluative judgment
Status of the reflective standpoint
No comprehensive non-natural realism assessment

name: The constitutive reply and its explicit scope
bridge_principles: Distinguishing willing from a succession of impulses requires commitments across relevantly similar possible occasions.
Endorsing a reason from a practical identity need not replace its other-directed content.
The rules of reflection constrain endorsement rather than making any choice correct.
conclusion: The reply offers formal universality and a response to reward-based interpretations; its full moral conclusion still depends on humanity and publicity arguments.
strongest_objection: Constitutive agency rules need independent defense; even granted general commitments, the all-persons domain and binding force of another’s reasons remain open.
strongest_reply: A rule internal to an activity need not be an arbitrary external command; the theory distinguishes genuine choice from impulse while retaining the content of concern for others.
unresolved_issues: Formal universality is not full moral universalism
Fully reflective endorsement and partial nonmoral obligations
Complete skepticism expressly left open

name: Enoch’s indispensability strategy: introduction, partial book text and direct author reply
position: For justified belief in irreducible normative truth
premises: Deliberation is rationally non-optional.
Normative truths and belief in them are instrumentally indispensable to that project.
bridge_principles: Indispensability to an appropriate non-optional project can justify ontological commitment; explanatory indispensability is a related instance.
conclusion: There is reason to believe irreducibly normative truths exist; a further moral bridge is needed.
source_locators: Google images pp.50–52/84; chapter4 and§5.1 limitations in A-P2T07-004/005
strongest_objection: Lenman's thin/thick dilemma challenges joint satisfaction of both premises.
strongest_reply: Enoch distinguishes merited standards, first-person warrant and value-sensitive instrumental indispensability.
unresolved_issues: Developed chapter3 pp.53–83, including epistemological defense, remain uninspected.
Chapter4 moral bridge and§5.1 now read; both are qualified and do not establish the missing derivation or premise truth.
Rejection of alternatives remains incomplete, explicitly at p.84 and§5.1.

name: Lenman's schmeliberation countercase
premises: Thin practical reflection uses scrutinized contingent concerns.
This activity admits success/error and deliberation-like phenomenology without robust truth.
Thickening it threatens non-optionality.
bridge_principles: A sufficient alternative defeats indispensability.
conclusion: Robust truths have not been shown indispensable to unavoidable deliberation.
strongest_objection: Standards and similarity may not supply the deserved allegiance claimed necessary.
strongest_reply: Lenman regards stable concerns and critical reflection as sufficient without further ratification of the whole.
unresolved_issues: Sufficiency of the thin project disputed.
Not every Humean or epistemic-normativity response inspected.
No empirical generalization from phenomenology.

name: Enoch's direct reply to schmeliberation
premises: Choosing versus picking is not proved exhaustive.
Formal standards may lack merited allegiance.
Replacement may preserve behavior while diminishing project value.
Justificatory evidence can vary without relativizing truth.
bridge_principles: A weaker replacement need not defeat the specified instrumental indispensability.
Phenomenology supplies claimed warrant, not truth-making.
conclusion: Lenman's alternative does not by itself remove Enoch's claimed reason to believe.
strongest_objection: Deserved allegiance may restate the disputed demand; private commitment needs a truth-directed epistemic bridge.
strongest_reply: Enoch invokes broader indispensability epistemology, permits premise error and distinguishes diminished projects from identical behavior.
unresolved_issues: Developed chapter3 vindication on pp.53–83 remains absent; opening and final p.84 are now read.
Expressivism response expressly preliminary at862.
Moorean criterion unsupplied863–864.
Color-blindness analogy is not validation.

name: Enoch’s conditional moral bridge
position: For extending justified general normative realism to robust moral realism, given moral objectivity
premises: Assume chapter 2 has established moral objectivity.
Assume chapter3 has supplied justified robust general normative realism, after objections have been considered.
Common objections concern normativity generally; moral facts are proposed to be of the same relevant ontological kind.
The chapter 4 response argues for a non-wholly-contingent connection between morality and reasons, explicitly limited to a weak claim.
bridge_principles: A disjunctive treatment of moral and other normative facts needs a rationale once shared objections and the proposed categorical-reason concern lose their force.
This is a defeasible motivation challenge, not entailment from the two antecedent conclusions.
conclusion: On those assumptions, familiar alternatives to robust moral realism are under-motivated; other unconsidered motivations remain possible.
strongest_objection: Shared objections can impose continuing costs, moral and other normativity may differ in relevant respects, and the antecedent chapter3 case has not been fully checked. Naturalist or expressivist alternatives may have further motivations.
strongest_reply: Enoch contrasts accumulating costs with an objection defeated at the level of kind, and argues that moral objectivity requires normative privilege rather than mere etiquette. He expressly limits the result to a weak moral-reason link and an open-ended challenge.
unresolved_issues: Antecedent objectivity and indispensability arguments not certified by this chapter’s reading
No guarantee of a reason in every case or overriding moral priority
Possible further rationale for a mixed or naturalist view; §5.1 remains open to successful reduction

name: Enoch’s qualified resistance to naturalist reduction
position: Defeasible initial suspicion of reduction with openness to successful detailed proposals
premises: From the deliberative standpoint, Enoch finds purely natural descriptions insufficient without normative background commitments.
Conceptual differences alone do not settle property identities, and a naturalist can claim the proposed base is itself normative.
Familiar a priori/a posteriori objections and the response to Schroeder are not a conclusive general irreducibility proof.
bridge_principles: An initial intuition can bear defeasible weight without being unrevisable.
Specific reductions must be assessed by their details and theoretical virtues; inability to refute one is not itself metaphysical evidence for it.
conclusion: Enoch retains suspicion but allows a strong specific, including token-level, reduction to overturn the initial commitment.
strongest_objection: The initial normative-force intuition may encode the disputed non-naturalism; the naturalist may accept concept difference while denying metaphysical difference.
strongest_reply: Enoch acknowledges this impasse and treats it as a limit on the argument, not a victory; he asks for detailed reductions capable of earning their theoretical costs and explicitly permits revising his intuition.
unresolved_issues: No separately inspected Schroeder original or full naturalism critic/reply chain
No supplied successful token-level theory; no refutation of all reductions
How the incomplete chapter3 indispensability case survives a reduction that preserves deliberation remains contested

name: Agreed biological tests and conditional theory defense
position: Retain the tests as challenges, while distinguishing auxiliary assumptions from full-theory refutation.
premises: The selected protocol fixes operational predictions and the final paper reports failures on some of them.
Antecedent conditional wording about conscious offset detection exists in the published protocol.
Proponents dispute awareness/attention, measurement scale and coverage; those disputes are not new independent data.
bridge_principles: Failure of a predicted measurement challenges the conjunction of theory, auxiliary implementation and measurement conditions.
A successful prediction shared by alternatives does not uniquely confirm one theory.
conclusion: Preserve a consequential but conditional empirical challenge; neither a whole-theory winner nor automatic dismissal is warranted.
strongest_objection: Auxiliary-condition defenses can insulate a theory against agreed failed tests; the collaboration was explicitly negotiated to avoid that flexibility.
strongest_reply: The offset condition predates results publication, and the papers acknowledge measurement and implementation limits; nevertheless source attribution alone does not show that any proposed explanation accounts for the observed failures.
unresolved_issues: Actual attention/continuous awareness at relevant times
How much each implementation is motivated by its core theory
No later consortium rebuttal identified under bounded search

name: Document chronology and compliance are separate questions
position: Narrow the v1 methods gap without certifying preregistration compliance.
premises: The December 2022 exact file states the thirds split and unsplit iEEG.
The February 2023 protocol contains different published half-split wording; its exact earlier wording/version timing has not been verified.
The 2025 supplement explicitly records deviations and inconsistent counts.
bridge_principles: Publication order is not necessarily protocol amendment order.
A public file version and hash establish document provenance more directly than actual analyst behavior.
conclusion: Qualify the historical wording; retain unresolved full history and execution audit, and label exploratory analyses correctly.
strongest_objection: An internally inconsistent ordinary OSF node is insufficient evidence for a clean prospective analysis history.
strongest_reply: Agreed; the limited finding is the dated exact document and stated methods, not clean compliance. The matching 2024 copy does not erase the 2022 version record.
unresolved_issues: Earlier amendment chain and actual data-access/code execution history were not audited
No earlier dated half-split original was reopened; different publication wording does not establish a change during the February 2023–April 2025 publication interval.

name: Do not substitute easier denominators
premises: Per-run volumes and overlapping windows differ from experimental runs or animals.
PET session/subframe totals differ from interview counts.
Selected appendix tables did not resolve the targeted numerator gaps.
bridge_principles: An evidential rate requires the corresponding numerator, denominator and sampling unit.
Repeated or overlapping observations do not by themselves increase the number of independent subjects.
conclusion: Retain scoped causal/association constraints while withholding reconstructed rates, precision upgrades and population generalizations.
strongest_objection: Raw files or another appendix may contain the missing totals, so bounded non-recovery is not a source-level absence proof.
strongest_reply: The packet explicitly preserves that distinction and requests the exact missing table/data fields rather than inventing the counts.
unresolved_issues: Animal-by-condition run and trial exclusions
Exact interview integer numerators/denominators and repeated-interview mapping

name: Conditional experiential-ultimate argument
premises: Experience exists as concrete reality.
For argument, concrete reality is physical and constituted by physical ultimates.
No experiential reality can emerge from wholly nonexperiential reality.
bridge_principles: Some ultimate constituents must therefore involve experience.
Homogeneity is an additional premise for all ultimates.
conclusion: Micropsychism, and panpsychism only with added homogeneity, conditional on the premises.
