strongest_objection: Goff: the supposedly explanatory experiential base still needs unexplained subject and quality combination; no-radical-emergence may be an asymmetrically applied intuition.
strongest_reply: Strawson: same-kind experiential composition may be incomprehensible to us without the metaphysical impossibility he attributes to the wholly nonexperiential case.
unresolved_issues: No independent validation of no-radical-emergence or homogeneity.
No constitution law or actual H-F test.

name: Goff’s combination and revelation challenge
premises: Many microsubjects do not transparently supply a further subject.
Strawson uses transparent experiential knowledge against ordinary a posteriori identifications.
If experiential being is exhaustively how it feels, a constituent’s experiential character must be part of the whole’s character.
bridge_principles: The needed transparency should apply to both nonexperiential-to-experiential and micro-to-macro transitions.
Wholly additive experiential parts cannot supply qualitatively novel wholes.
conclusion: The proposed panpsychism has not escaped brute emergence; under the stronger transparency/parthood assumptions novel experiential combination is incoherent.
strongest_objection: The transparency premise may exceed first-order acquaintance in certain respects; experiential constitution need not be additive or perspective-sharing.
strongest_reply: Goff: without sufficient transparency, Strawson must explain why ignorance does not equally protect physicalist reduction; footnote 2 extends the concern to experiential nature generally.
unresolved_issues: Goff’s strongest impossibility conclusion is conditional on contested bridges.
James and Loar antecedents uninspected.

name: Partial acquaintance and active experiential constitution
premises: One has first-order acquaintance with one’s experience without knowing every causal or constitutive feature.
Constituting microsubjects are numerically distinct and need not share their perspectives with the macrosubject.
Experiences are active realities, not passive contents isolated from causal powers.
bridge_principles: Absence of a constituent’s phenomenal character in acquaintance need not establish absence of an experiential constituent.
conclusion: One full-revelation argument for impossibility can be resisted while experiential composition remains a conditional possibility requiring further account.
strongest_objection: The revised ontology and ignorance allowance do not explain composition and may weaken the original exclusion of nonexperiential emergence.
strongest_reply: Strawson acknowledges the concession, rejects exhaustive revelation in the relevant sense, and relies on a transcendental argument with smallism.
unresolved_issues: His pp. 258–259 argument is acknowledged defective.
No positive law specifying subjects, qualities, organization or causal realization.
No later Goff rebuttal invented.

name: Equal explanatory standards and component limits
premises: Source-verified attributions do not verify premises.
A conditional experiential ontology can fit neural dependence without a disembodied enduring subject.
Accepted P2T01 and P2T02 supply developed alternatives with distinct unresolved costs.
bridge_principles: Do not confuse constitutive dependence, diachronic causal generation, intrinsic-property identity and distinct-subject ontology.
Require actuality and separate bridges for each component.
conclusion: Retain experiential constitution as a specified conditional alternative; withhold six-family ranking and all conclusion gates.
strongest_objection: A defender might regard no-radical-emergence and acquaintance as sufficiently decisive for actual panpsychism.
strongest_reply: The selected reply explicitly acknowledges intuitive premises, unknown composition and optional universal-subject extension.
unresolved_issues: Exact 2006 lead still unavailable.
Broader literature and empirical discriminators not completed.

name: EEG–recollection intersection challenge and direct reply

Absence of explicit memory is not equivalent to absence of consciousness.

premises: Experiential reality requires explanation and economy favors one kind if adequate.

Bodies/perception are posited as appearances and cross-boundary influences of cosmic experiential patterns.

Access/impingement structure realizes the required subject and qualitative facts.

name: Conditional cosmic subject-constitution objection
premises: Cosmic subject and all its cosmic mental states can seemingly be conceived without further distinct macrosubjects.
Constitution requires the subject facts to be fixed by the ground.
bridge_principles: Relevant conceivability entails metaphysical possibility.
Grounding entails relevant necessitation.

name: Plural substantial unity and internally lawful representation
premises: Composites require genuine simples.
Mechanical aggregates do not explain perception.
Each monad has an intrinsic representational nature and qualitative individuality.
God creates and coordinates substances and their laws.
bridge_principles: Unity requires non-composite active bearers.
Divine coordination grounds consistent representations and ordinary causal descriptions without influx.
conclusion: Plural created perceivers express one world without forming one numerically identical subject.
strongest_objection: Foucher questions unextended foundations, organic/mental unity, and why externally coordinated bodies are needed if appearances are internally sufficient.

name: Unnecessary bodies and post hoc coordination
premises: Synchronized bodily/mental sequences are possible.
Soul appearances could seem the same without appropriate bodies or motions.
A theory built to save prior separations may not be independently justified.
bridge_principles: Explanatory economy and epistemic justification favor avoiding unnecessary untested entities.
Effort/resistance may permit interaction unless excluded by defended premises.
conclusion: Leibniz owes justification for bodies and harmony beyond possible coordination.
strongest_objection: Leibniz says harmony follows from true unities, laws are internal, and God values more substances with external correspondence.
strongest_reply: Leibniz’s actual1696reply treats harmony as law-grounded rather than recurring intervention, permits revised ordinary causal language, and defends a priori reasons plus empirical fit.

name: Abductive case for a nonphenomenal account
premises: Apparent phenomenality motivates explanation; realists and illusionists dispute what this appearance warrants.
Fallible representation could in principle generate phenomenal judgments without their proposed qualitative referents.
If a sufficiently adequate nonphenomenal account is available, theoretical economy can favor it.
bridge_principles: B-P2T05-01: Explanatory economy tracks the relevant truth only given adequate coverage and no stronger independently justified target datum.
B-P2T05-02: Psychological/representational explanation can capture the relevant epistemic achievement, not merely duplicate an utterance.
conclusion: Frankish infers that phenomenal realism is mistaken and favors illusionism; his practical recommendation is to develop the programme. This attribution does not establish the abductive premises or their truth-conduciveness.
strongest_objection: A-P2T05-002 disputes that the target is exhausted by fallible representations and asks whether the economy argument starts from a distorted target.
strongest_reply: A-P2T05-003 contests whether ostension fixes the target’s realist nature and returns the burden to an account of unmediated awareness.

name: Experiential target, reference and immediate awareness
premises: Phenomenal consciousness concerns subjects undergoing experiential properties; an event-property description may distort the target.
Examples can establish reference without making their nature depend on a philosophical description.
On her account, undergoing an experiential property is already awareness of it; no additional representation is needed.
At least one relevant experiential example is actually instantiated.
bridge_principles: B-P2T05-03: The ostensively fixed experiential target includes the relevant what-it-is-like aspect without a theory-laden phenomenal-property premise.
B-P2T05-04: Immediate awareness is identical with experiential instantiation in the relevant sense and cannot be simulated by a merely functional seeming.
conclusion: Given the stated exemplification and target premises, denial of experiential consciousness fails; the argument is conditional, as her§4 explicitly says.
strongest_objection: A-P2T05-003 accepts the examples and commonality but disputes that they rule out a nonphenomenal interpretation; rejecting PPP alone cannot block a recast illusionist claim.
strongest_reply: Her§2 p7 supplies the immediate-awareness argument, and§3 p9 distinguishes misdescribing a real property from denying its instantiation. These address more than a bare assertion that consciousness exists.
unresolved_issues: This paper’s short explanations do not inspect its cited fuller2016a/2016b accounts.
The premise identifying awareness with instantiation cannot be certified by the author’s conviction.
Opposition does not contradict the attribution records.

name: Reply: reference need not settle nature
position: Frankish’s actual response to the selected critic
premises: Grant the subject-property recasting for argument.
Accept ordinary examples and a shared feature while interpreting that feature through representational states and dispositions.
Ostension need not guarantee the descriptive or metaphysical nature attributed to its target.
bridge_principles: B-P2T05-05: The proposed nonphenomenal interpretation is a live explanation of the very target introduced, rather than a substitute phenomenon.
B-P2T05-06: Cognitive access to structural/dispositional physical properties requires mediation; direct acquaintance cannot independently settle the question.
conclusion: Reference fixing alone does not rule out his illusionist ontology; the remaining immediate-awareness disagreement reaches explicitly acknowledged metaphysical commitments.
strongest_objection: Nida-Rümelin’s positive awareness premise targets B-P2T05-05/06: preserving verbal examples need not preserve the experiential property she points to.
strongest_reply: He does not merely deny the examples: he specifies an alternative account of their commonality. His physicalist refusal of robust acquaintance is candidly qualified as unpersuasive to this critic.
unresolved_issues: The reply does not supply a neutral proof that Nida-Rümelin’s target is entirely captured.
Physicalist motivation is not an independently established premise.
No subsequent Nida-Rümelin response was required or established by these searches.

name: Illusion, regress and the remaining content burden
position: Strong sourced challenge and the selected author’s replies
premises: If the supposed illusion itself has phenomenal character, phenomenality has not been eliminated.
If it is only a coarse belief, the account may fail to explain experiential richness.
If each apparent feel requires a higher phenomenal representation, the explanation risks regress or a concealed phenomenal starting point.
bridge_principles: B-P2T05-07: An illusion of phenomenality needs the relevant phenomenal seeming; this must be argued, not assumed from the everyday word illusion.
B-P2T05-08: The offered nonphenomenal representations can explain content, richness and reactions without a conscious internal audience.
conclusion: The regress objection identifies a real explanatory constraint; it is not automatically a contradiction once functional seeming and limited introspection are allowed.
strongest_objection: Merely renaming a state a nonphenomenal representation does not explain why it presents determinate apparent qualities or captures what the critic means by experience.
strongest_reply: Original§§3.2–3.4 rejects phenomenal content vehicles and inner observers; reply pp9–10 allows a limited higher-order route; p23 allows fine-grained nonphenomenal states. None is claimed as a completed mechanism.

The Prinz/Pereboom alternatives are seen through Frankish’s reply; their originals remain uninspected.
A modal prohibition on functional seeming and an adequate worked model remain distinct unresolved demands.

name: From possible explanation to actual explanation of the maximal contingent fact
premises: Admissible world-complete BCCFs, maximality, bivalence and compossibility.
W-PSR: every proposition true at any possible world can obtain with an explanation.
bridge_principles: A world containing the complete actual BCCF must be the actual world.
Truth-preserving inference within that framework.
conclusion: Conditionally, the actual BCCF has an actual explanation.
strongest_objection: Oppy: universal W-PSR entails the strong principle under explanatory assumptions; weaker counterpart intuitions do not warrant the world-complete premise, and informed rational dissent can remain.

name: From total explanation to a necessary free agent and its attributes
premises: An actual totality explanation is available under A-P2T10-001.
Personal/scientific explanation exhausts the intelligible options.
Contingent explanantia cannot explain themselves, while a necessary being’s libertarian action can terminate explanation.
Genuine contingency rules out necessitating creative action.
bridge_principles: Exclude scientific and contingent-agent explanations.
Treat necessary existence and contingent free action separately.
Add teleological evidence and further theodicy for power, intelligence and goodness.
conclusion: Conditionally, a necessary free agent creates the actual universe; rich qualities require further arguments.
strongest_objection: The defender’s reported Quinn alternative is an impersonal indeterministic necessary source; the strongest project question is why libertarian self-explanation is sufficient when impersonal indeterminism is not, given context-sensitive explanatory fullness.
strongest_reply: Gale and Pruss argue that only free action can be an indeterministic self-explainer, appeal to cosmic order, and offer a generic necessary powerful cause fallback (p472).

premises: Explanation is veridical and dissective under the stated modal logic.
W-PSR applies to an obtaining conjunction that says a fact obtains and is unexplained.
Some non-theists have independently rational grounds that conflict with the conclusion.
bridge_principles: Explaining the conjunction produces the conditional reductio.
Logical entailment does not settle which belief should be revised; initial assent may have been uninformed.
conclusion: The advertised weakness advantage is not established by those premises; rational rejection can remain.
strongest_objection: The2002 reply grants entailment but argues that incomplete deductive knowledge can coexist with adequate understanding, that evil does not defeat every necessary creator, and that W-PSR better coheres with inquiry (pp90–97).

premises: Mechanism and agent can explain different aspects of an artifact.

Such order and rational capacities are asserted to fit creative intelligence.

Freely owning and improving love may be goods.
For selected dispositions, withholding belief may be no worse a means than available alternatives.

Epistemic restraint about unknown reasons differs from proof of a sufficient actual reason.

position: Schellenberg’s structural reply and the surviving epistemic dispute
premises: There may be positive defeasible support that a perfectly loving God intends the relevant access.

name: Final loss and the necessity of endurance
position: Reconstructed strict necessity rationale; neither Yoshizawa nor Metz endorses its soundness
premises: Ordinary relationships and activities can be valuable.
Death ends a person and may end valued relationships.
The strict advocate claims the ending makes the whole life meaningless.
bridge_principles: Ending must negate relevant whole-life significance, not merely preclude additional goods.
The meaning at issue and its temporal bearer must be specified.
conclusion: The third premise would require endurance for meaning only if the loss-to-meaninglessness bridge is defended.
strongest_objection: Yoshizawa distinguishes no existing subject from an existing subject without meaning, and past meaning from present instantiation; strict necessity does not follow from an ending.

name: Possible worthwhile continuation with ownership and engagement
premises: Some activities can remain worthwhile or repeatable.
A future life can contain varied goods and changes acceptable through reflection.
The future experiences must belong to the same person and remain appropriately attractive.
bridge_principles: Finite repeatability must extend to the proposed duration.
Future subjectivity and identity must actually obtain for survival.
Possible appeal does not establish all endless lives good.

strongest_objection: Williams’s stronger concern is exhausted categorical projects or a remote life not appropriately related to the present person; ordinary repetition may fail indefinitely.
strongest_reply: Fischer distinguishes repeatable from self-exhausting goods, permits a varied life and appropriate character changes, and separates absorption from ownership.
unresolved_issues: Williams original is frozen accepted derivative, not fresh reading.
No infinite aggregate-value measure, empirical immortality or survival inference.

name: Finite value, ultimate context and intended purpose
position: Several conditional questions; no forced metaphysical winner
premises: Worthwhile engagement can be evaluated at the level of an individual life.

Descriptive occurrence must not become intention.
A divine theory’s possibility is distinct from its actuality or necessity.

The 2000 original itself already leaves two response strategies open and does not claim the objection requires disbelief (p311).

premises: Laxity range parameter x is uncertain.

Use defined proper priors or explicitly qualified limiting ratios, preserving normalization and endpoint terms.
